description: Baseline geometry planner: 32/50 successes with 25 remote workers.

asi.hypothesis: Current fixed straight-arm geometry is a measurable baseline; failures cluster at grasp and transport.
asi.run_integrity: 45/50 terminal results; 5 seeds missing, so success count is conservative.
asi.next_action: Honor user request: rerun with 10 workers, then redesign geometry rather than tune small thresholds.

description: Benchmark with requested 10 workers: 36/50 successes, all 50 terminal results.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing concurrency makes benchmark complete and improves measured outcomes, but grasp and transport remain dominant planner failures.
asi.next_action: Inspect failure-stage distribution and redesign end-to-end geometry, not threshold/retry micro-fixes.

description: Tried 65-degree shoulder-pan and live TCP-to-base parking; 12/50, worse than 36/50.

asi.hypothesis: Moving shoulder pan far inward and recomputing base offset would improve IK margin.
asi.result: False: grasp success collapsed and transport/placement counts fell; fixed straight-arm 85-degree geometry is important for downstream reach.
asi.next_action: Revert; use measured pre-grasp arm pose while retaining 85-degree transport geometry. Redesign final grasp orientation/approach instead of global pan change.

description: Added alternate front-facing live-geometry grasp after straight-arm grasp fails: 38/50.

asi.hypothesis: Initial failures were invalid wrist orientation, not just distance; a horizontal front grasp reconstructed from live TCP-to-cup vector should recover them without perturbing successful runs.
asi.result: Improved 36→38; all runs complete. Remaining failures should be analyzed at regrasp, transport, and lift/evaluation stages.
asi.next_action: Use same geometric grasp-frame idea for tray regrasp and replace coarse transport target with payload-centered route.
